sections.h2: Arvada housing and which county you are in
sections.html:
Arvada sits about 7 miles northwest of downtown Denver. It had 124,402 residents in 2020 and an estimate of 121,873 in 2024. Nearly all of it is in Jefferson County, where 121,510 of those residents live, with a small slice in Adams County. Your tax bill names the county that applies to your house.

A lot of the housing arrived with suburban growth after World War II. Older neighborhoods cluster around Olde Town Arvada, and newer subdivisions sit toward the edges. Jefferson County School District R-1 covers the Jefferson County side, and Westminster Public Schools covers the Adams County side. On an older home, buyers and inspectors go straight to the roof, the furnace and the sewer line, so look at those before you pick a price.

Valuation comes from Jefferson County and collection from the Jefferson County Treasurer, at 100 Jefferson County Parkway, Suite 2520, in Golden. The number is 303-271-8330, and the office is closed Fridays.

Payment optionDue date
First halfLast day of February
Second halfJune 15
Full paymentApril 30
  • A bill above $25 may be paid in halves, while anything smaller is due in full by April 30.
  • Residential assessment rates for 2026: 6.8% for local governments, 7.05% for schools.
  • Odd-numbered years bring a revaluation, with notices out by May 1.
  • Standard state schedule puts the protest deadline at June 8, though your own notice has the final word.

Each January 1, a tax lien attaches to any county property with taxes owing. Taxes still unpaid in late October send that lien to the county's annual sale, and the owner then gets three years to redeem.

The timeline bites hardest when a balance has sat for a year or longer. Find out from the Treasurer where the account stands before you accept an offer, so a lien does not surprise the title company later.

The city permits stays of under 30 days at a short-term rental, provided the owner holds a city license. The annual registration fee was reported at $150 in early 2025, and city staff said many rentals operated without a license: more than 800 rentals, and only about 250 to 300 holding a license.

A former guest rental can carry licensing or complaint history, and a buyer may want proof. Round up the license, any city notices and the tax filings first.

Three routes are open: hire an agent, sell it yourself, or take a cash offer for the house as is. Listing tends to mean repairs, showings and weeks spent waiting on a buyer's loan.

Cash fits an inherited house, a vacant rental, put-off repairs or a short deadline. The county clerk records the deed, and tax owed comes out of the proceeds.

Send us your Arvada address and we will lay out the choices before you commit to anything.

sections.h2: What happens to the tax bill at closing
sections.html:
Your title company requests a Certificate of Taxes Due from the Jefferson County Treasurer, and its figure lands on the settlement statement. Any balance is subtracted from your proceeds, so owing tax does not mean bringing money to the table.

  1. Name the county your parcel is in when you open the file.
  2. Scan the certificate for balances from earlier years.
  3. If a lien shows, verify the payoff at 303-271-8330.
  4. At signing, the balance is paid from your side of the ledger.

Golden is a drive from Arvada and the office is shut Fridays, so pick another weekday for a visit or leave it to the title company.

sections.h2: Challenging your valuation before a sale
sections.html:
Planning a spring sale? Read your valuation notice. Notices go out by May 1 in a revaluation year, which comes every other year. The standard state schedule allows protests until June 8, but some counties run an alternate schedule, so trust the date printed on your notice.

A lower assessed value will not set your sale price, though it lowers the bill from then on, and a buyer's agent may look at it. Collect comparable sales and photos of condition problems before filing. Value questions go to the Jefferson County Assessor. Bills and payments go to the Treasurer at 303-271-8330.

sections.h2: How a cash sale works here
sections.html:
A cash sale moves faster than a listing, yet the paperwork matches. Here is the normal order.

  1. Share your Arvada address, a few details about the house and what you owe.
  2. We walk through how a sale would go and which tax numbers title will want.
  3. Once terms are agreed, title opens a file and orders the tax certificate.
  4. Taxes and liens are paid out of your proceeds when you close.
  5. The county clerk records the deed and you are finished.

Nobody tours the house and no buyer's loan has to be approved. That works for a property with put-off repairs, a vacant rental, an inheritance or a hard deadline.

Guest-rental owners have a little more to line up. Pull the city license if you had one, plus any notices the city sent about the property, and collect the tax filings tied to the rental income. A clean file lets a buyer or title company move faster than one that has to keep asking.

If the rental ran without a license, consider how that history reads on paper before you list. City staff have said unlicensed owners are hard to find because many hold property through an LLC, which is part of why the city watches the issue. Tidy records answer questions before they become delays.

Inherited and empty houses often carry several open items together: a tax balance, an old loan, repairs nobody made. Selling for cash as is settles them from the proceeds in a single closing so you do not fix each one first. Learn what is owed by calling the Treasurer, then decide whether a listing or a direct sale suits your timeline.

sections.h2: Before you list: a short checklist
sections.html:
• Locate the last tax statement and note the county on it.
  • Learn how old the roof, furnace and sewer line are, because buyers will ask.
  • Ask your insurance agent about hail and wind coverage, since an open claim can complicate a closing.
  • A guest rental calls for the license and any city notices.
  • Get payoff figures for every loan and any tax balance.

Put the folder together once and reuse it, whether you list, sell by owner or take a cash offer. A seller who can answer questions about the roof, the tax account and the loan payoff on the same day keeps momentum, and momentum matters when a deadline is near.

A cash buyer wants most of these facts too, without a lender's appraisal or repair list in the way.

faqs.a: Mostly Jefferson County, with a small part (2,892 residents in 2020) in Adams County. The tax bill shows which applies to you.

faqs.q: What is the Arvada property tax protest deadline?
faqs.a: Under the standard state schedule the protest deadline is June 8. Read your own Notice of Valuation, since counties can use an alternate schedule.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Arvada house with unpaid property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. Closing pays back taxes from your proceeds, and the title company gets the exact amount from the Jefferson County Treasurer.

faqs.q: Are short-term rentals allowed in Arvada?
faqs.a: Yes, with a license. The annual fee was reported at $150 in early 2025, and staff said many rentals were unlicensed.
Jefferson County School District R-1 covers the Jefferson County side, and Westminster Public Schools covers the Adams County side.
